title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction
domain: single-cell transcriptomics; developmental dynamics and genetic perturbation prediction
dataset_or_cohort: Pretraining: seven public mouse embryonic datasets aggregated into ten leaf trajectories; downstream: Weinreb hematopoiesis, Veres islet differentiation, Norman Perturb-seq, and CellStream EMT/MOSTA analyses
sample_scale: 2,477,217 pretraining cells across 135 files, ten leaf trajectories, and 88 sampled timepoints; downstream sample counts not reported in the inspected paper
institution_count: NA: public multi-study cell atlases; contributing institution count and geography were not enumerated
split_strategy: Held-out downstream datasets were excluded from both pretraining stages; downstream comparisons used common task-specific train/test splits, but exact split proportions were not reported
observation_process: Destructive scRNA-seq population snapshots across developmental time; unpaired source and target cells; normalized counts encoded into a shared scVI latent
missingness: Gene space harmonized to 16,520 mouse-human one-to-one orthologs, with 35 aliases; normalize_total(10^4) plus log1p; cell-level missingness was not modeled as an observation process
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: population-snapshot tasks without patient discharge, death, or dropout; no competing-event model
state: 128-dimensional scVI latent transcriptional state over a fixed ortholog vocabulary; source population, elapsed time, optional action token, and stochastic noise
observation_decoder: One-step future latent-cell population, optionally decoded to gene expression; downstream outputs also include clonal fate scores and GEARS perturbation predictions
action: Optional intervention token in the architecture; genetic knockout identity is handled only through the downstream GEARS embedding-replacement experiment
action_provenance: The temporal-pretraining action token is null; Norman CRISPR perturbations are observed experimental labels processed by GEARS, not by a demonstrated standalone Chreode action encoder
transition_mechanism: Single-pass additive Waddington-DiT residual combining a potential gradient, antisymmetric flow, and learned stochastic spread with an elapsed-time gate
maximum_horizon: One model step for any supplied elapsed time; evaluated from Weinreb day 2 to days 4 and 6 and from Veres time 0 to seven target timepoints; no recursive rollout
rollout_regime: Single-pass one-step prediction; no teacher-forced or free-running recursive rollout
capability_claim: Claims an action-conditioned one-step cell transition and perturbation prediction; evidence directly supports passive temporal population forecasting and transferable dynamics representations, but not a standalone action-conditioned perturbation operator, counterfactual validity, planning, or rollout
baselines: Matched scratch W-DiT, PI-SDE, PRESCIENT, identity/source replay, linear time-delta, static-DiT, GEARS official, scVI replacement, scDiffEq, moscot, WOT, CellStream, and architectural/training ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: Sinkhorn W2 and MMD in shared latent space; decoded gene-space DE20 MSE and Pearson correlations; clonal-fate Pearson correlation; velocity consistency
transition_metrics: Per-target Sinkhorn W2 at Weinreb days 4/6 and Veres times 1-7; endpoint and average W2; fate correlation; DE20 perturbation-prediction error
rollout_stability: No free-running stability test; one-step performance is reported at multiple elapsed times, and time-embedding/multi-delta ablations examine long-delta one-step behavior
action_sensitivity: No action removal, shuffle, timing, dose, or action-agnostic comparator for Chreode's action token; GEARS embedding arms isolate representation transfer rather than action sensitivity
calibration_and_uncertainty: K stochastic samples and a learned per-dimension noise scale are used, but the paper explicitly reports no calibrated uncertainty or credible-interval evaluation
external_validation: Held-out downstream datasets and cross-species tasks are evaluated, but time-transition and GEARS perturbation results use downstream fine-tuning or adaptation; only the Weinreb clonal-fate analysis uses the frozen pretrained backbone with no downstream training. No wet-lab, adult-human-tissue, or clinical validation.
decision_utility: No clinician, policy, screening, or control decision evaluation; downstream tasks are forecasting, representation, and fate/perturbation prediction
safety_evaluation: A qualitative dual-use discussion is provided, but no defined biological hazard, severity, failure stress test, constraint, override, or monitoring evaluation is reported
statistical_analysis: Mean and sample standard deviation over three downstream seeds for many results; pretraining uses one checkpoint; several tables report descriptive differences without formal hypothesis tests or confidence intervals
causal_language: Uses intervention and do(a) notation and calls the model action-conditioned, while explicitly stating that the world-model analogy is predictive only and that planning or rollout is not claimed
estimand: A conditional future-population distribution indexed by state, elapsed time, and nominal intervention is written; no population treatment-effect contrast, regime value, or individual counterfactual estimand is identified
confounding_strategy: No confounding adjustment or causal design; developmental snapshots and perturbation labels are used for predictive training
positivity_and_overlap: No positivity or overlap analysis for interventions; the fixed ortholog vocabulary addresses feature compatibility, not treatment support
counterfactual_validation: None; held-out observed populations and perturbation labels validate prediction, not unobserved counterfactual trajectories
code_access: An anonymized code repository in supplementary material is reported, but no stable inspectable repository URL is present in the inspected arXiv PDF
weights_access: Pretrained weights explicitly not released with the submission
data_access: All named pretraining and downstream datasets are public under source-specific terms; accession identifiers are listed
preprocessing_reproducibility: Substantial detail for ortholog construction, normalization, scVI and W-DiT architecture, losses, optimizer, horizons, and metrics; exact downstream split construction and an externally inspectable code path remain incomplete
randomness: One pretraining seed; downstream evaluation uses three seeds controlling splits/noise; K=8 training and K=32 evaluation samples
evidence_anchors: Abstract and pp. 2-7 for claim, model, pretraining corpus, and protocol; Tables 1-4 on pp. 8-9; Scope on pp. 9-10; Appendices A-C and Tables 5-6 on pp. 12-15; uncertainty limitation on p. 16; ablations on pp. 17-18; NeurIPS checklist pp. 19-25
appraisal_strengths: Large multi-dataset pretraining corpus; explicit one-step scope boundary; multiple downstream datasets; matched architecture controls; per-target temporal results and architecture/training ablations
appraisal_limitations: Action token is null during temporal pretraining and not evaluated downstream; perturbation evidence comes from embedding replacement inside GEARS; no rollout, calibration, broad frozen external validation, or causal identification; only the zero-shot Weinreb fate analysis is frozen, and exact downstream split details are incomplete
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: Clin-JEPA: A Multi-Phase Co-Training Framework for Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining on EHR Patient Trajectories
domain: ICU electronic health records; latent patient-trajectory forecasting and multi-task risk prediction
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV ICU with raw tables and official mimic-code derived concepts
sample_scale: 84,497 ICU stays from 64,874 unique patients; approximately 197,000 training windows; 10,346 test stays for the stay-level benchmark
institution_count: One health system/source database: Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center MIMIC-IV
split_strategy: Patient-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split; all stays from a patient remain together; stays longer than 72 hours yield overlapping windows with 12-hour stride
observation_process: Irregular vital, laboratory, severity, medication, procedure, and device events serialized into one-hour natural-language state/action fragments while preserving within-hour event order
missingness: No numerical imputation or normalization; absent readings are omitted from state text, so missingness is represented implicitly by absence rather than explicitly modeled
censoring_or_competing_events: ICU windows are capped at 72 hours and long stays are windowed; no censoring, discharge, death, or competing-event process is modeled in the latent transition
state: 4096-dimensional Qwen3-8B last-token embeddings for demographics, hourly state text, and hourly action text; historical and predicted latent states form the patient representation
observation_decoder: Absolute next-state latent embedding; autoregressive latent trajectory; shallow probes output risks for 15 downstream tasks; no observation reconstruction decoder
action: Hourly active interventions and doses, including vasopressors, ventilation, dialysis, procedures, fluids, medication orders, and administrations
action_provenance: Observed EHR interventions from derived treatment concepts and raw inputevents, procedureevents, prescriptions, and eMAR; provenance mixes orders, administrations, settings, and active treatments
transition_mechanism: A 92.5M-parameter block-causal Transformer predicts absolute next-state embeddings and recursively feeds its own continuous predictions back into the state sequence
maximum_horizon: 48-hour evaluated autoregressive rollout from a 24-hour context; source windows extend to 72 hours
rollout_regime: Teacher forcing plus a two-step rollout loss during training; fully autoregressive free-running latent rollout at inference and in the 48-hour drift evaluation
capability_claim: Action-conditioned latent patient-trajectory forecasting/simulation and reusable risk representation; no causal alternative-treatment, counterfactual, or planning evidence
baselines: V-JEPA 2-AC-style encoder/predictor, SFT-only encoder, curriculum ablations without warmup/alignment, Ridge, LightGBM, LSTM, and TCN
state_fidelity_metrics: Encoder temporal standard deviation, UMAP cohort trajectories, centroid displacement ratios, Mann-Whitney tests, Cohen's d, and downstream AUROC/AUPRC
transition_metrics: L1 distance between autoregressive predicted latent state and the true encoder state over 48 hours, normalized to horizon 1
rollout_stability: Horizon-by-horizon normalized L1 drift with mean, median, and IQR; representation-collapse trajectories; only the complete curriculum converges rather than accumulates drift
action_sensitivity: Actions are included as predictor inputs, but no action-agnostic comparator, removal, shuffle, timing, dose, or path-substitution test is reported
calibration_and_uncertainty: Deterministic conditional-mean rollout; no predictive distribution, calibration, interval coverage, abstention, or uncertainty-aware decision rule
external_validation: No external, temporal, institutional, geographic, device, or population validation; all training and evaluation use MIMIC-IV
decision_utility: Offline shallow-probe utility on seven early-event and eight stay-level risk tasks; no clinician workflow, treatment policy, or prospective decision evaluation
safety_evaluation: No clinical hazard definition, harmful-recommendation analysis, subgroup worst-case safety test, override, or monitoring evaluation
statistical_analysis: Per-task 95% bootstrap confidence intervals from 500 stay-clustered resamples; one-sided Mann-Whitney U tests and Cohen's d for latent geometry; training uses a single reported seed
causal_language: Describes a patient-state simulator conditioned on a proposed action sequence, but does not use causal, treatment-effect, counterfactual, or policy-value claims
estimand: Observed-policy next-latent-state prediction and downstream risk classification; no intervention contrast or regime-value estimand
confounding_strategy: No causal confounding strategy; actions are predictive covariates in the recorded EHR
counterfactual_validation: None; autoregressive predictions are compared with observed future embeddings and labels only
code_access: Public GitHub repository linked in the paper and inspectable at coding cutoff
weights_access: Study-specific trained checkpoint access is not established in the paper; the external Qwen3-8B base model is separately available under its source terms
data_access: MIMIC-IV requires credentialed PhysioNet access; source tables and feature inventory are specified
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed eligibility, patient split, hourly serialization, feature tables, architecture, five-phase schedule, optimizer, compute, probe protocol, and bootstrap procedures
randomness: Random seed 42; one reported training run; bootstrap resampling is specified
evidence_anchors: Abstract and pp. 2-6 for claims, state/action encoding, transition, and curriculum; Fig. 2 and Sec. 5.2 pp. 6-7 for 48-hour rollout; Fig. 3 pp. 8-9 for state geometry; Fig. 4 and Sec. 5.4 p. 9; Appendices A-D pp. 13-18 for features, hyperparameters, ablations, and confidence intervals
appraisal_strengths: Clear patient-disjoint split; explicit free-running 48-hour evaluation; strong failure-mode ablations; direct latent-state and downstream task evidence; detailed feature and training appendices; public code
appraisal_limitations: Single-source retrospective data; no action-sensitivity test despite action-conditioned framing; no calibration, external validation, causal identification, clinical decision study, or safety evaluation; only one reported training seed
source_status: Primary arXiv v4 full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories
domain: ICU physiological time-series forecasting with observed vasopressor conditioning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV v3.1 development cohort and independently processed eICU-CRD v2.0 replication cohort
sample_scale: MIMIC-IV: 40,301 stays (28,210 train, 6,045 validation, 6,046 test); eICU: 55,093 stays (38,633 train, 8,115 validation, 8,345 test)
institution_count: MIMIC-IV is single-center; eICU test data span 131 hospitals and 212 hospital-ward pairs, all represented in training
split_strategy: Patient-disjoint MIMIC splits; patient-level 70/15/15 eICU hash split; independent preprocessing and training by database; eICU is cross-database but not hospital-held-out
observation_process: Twenty-seven physiological variables in one-hour bins with observation masks, elapsed times, time features, static context, and a future candidate vasopressor path
missingness: Past-only within-stay forward filling; remaining leading gaps use training-set medians; masks and elapsed times are retained; eICU mappings and normalization are fit on eICU training data only
censoring_or_competing_events: Adults with ICU length of stay at least 24 hours; first eligible stay retained; pre-index vasopressor exposure and death by hour 6 excluded; trajectories limited to first 72 ICU hours; no censoring or competing-risk model
state: Normalized 27-variable physiology plus masks, elapsed times, history encoding, direct latent states, recursively advanced latent states, time features, and static predictive context
observation_decoder: A shared decoder outputs all 27 future variables, followed by a local correction for HR, SBP, DBP, and MAP
action: Hourly binary exposure to any of dopamine, epinephrine, norepinephrine, phenylephrine, or vasopressin, encoded with exposure, onset, duration, and time since exposure
action_provenance: Recorded administered/input-event vasopressor exposure in MIMIC; positive infusion snapshots with a 120-minute carry in eICU; supplied paths are observed or donor-substituted predictive scenarios
transition_mechanism: Hybrid direct-recursive model: a TFT-style direct anchor predicts all future states, while a shared one-hour recursive latent transition supplies bounded low-dimensional corrections through a shared decoder
maximum_horizon: Up to 48 hours, with results at 8, 24, and 48 hours and integrated lead-wise evaluation over hours 1-48
rollout_regime: One call returns the full trajectory; the direct path is multi-output and causal in the action prefix, while an internal recursive state consumes its own preceding latent state hourly; the recursive path is never decoded independently
capability_claim: Action-conditioned factual forecasting; the paper explicitly rejects causal treatment-effect, counterfactual, policy, action-generation, and recommendation interpretations
baselines: Persistence, GRU with/without action, mask-decay GRU, Transformer with/without action, TFT with/without dynamic action, capacity-matched TFT-Large, forecast-loss-transfer TFT-Large-FL, PatchTST-action, iTransformer-action, PPO-inspired DirRecMO-8, and seven component ablations
state_fidelity_metrics: Normalized endpoint and integrated 27-variable MSE; raw and observed-only MAP MAE; HR/SBP/DBP/MAP MAE; subgroup directional counts
transition_metrics: Endpoint MSE and MAP MAE at 8/24/48 hours; integrated 1-48-hour trajectory errors; recursive-direct latent discrepancy, final-direct MSE, and correction RMS by lead
rollout_stability: Horizon-specific and integrated trajectory errors; latent discrepancy and correction magnitude at leads 1, 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, and 48; changed-path prediction response aligned to first divergence
action_sensitivity: Action/no-action baselines; full-stream and future-only donor-path replacement; changed-window analyses; first-divergence timing; removal of recursive response/timing; residual-budget sensitivity
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive uncertainty, formal calibration, interval coverage, or abstention; confidence intervals quantify comparative sampling uncertainty only
external_validation: Independent eICU database replication with source-specific retraining and preprocessing; all test hospitals and wards occur in training, and the model is adapted rather than frozen
decision_utility: No clinician, treatment-policy, recommendation, or prospective workflow evaluation; utility is forecasting accuracy and input-dependence auditing
safety_evaluation: No clinical hazard/severity framework or intervention-safety test; exploratory subgroup reversals are descriptive and not a safety evaluation
statistical_analysis: Three seeds (42-44); 2,000 or 5,000 hierarchical bootstrap samples over seeds and stays; plus-one two-sided probabilities; Benjamini-Hochberg correction; shared checkpoint-selection robustness; confidence intervals reported
causal_language: Explicitly states that actions are predictive covariates, DRIFT estimates neither a policy nor counterfactual outcomes, replacement audits input dependence, and results do not establish causal effects or clinical benefit
estimand: Recorded-path factual trajectory prediction and shifted-input error-gap comparisons with the observed outcome held fixed; no intervention-effect or regime-value estimand
confounding_strategy: Two treatment-likelihood features are fitted on training data as predictive context only and are not causal weights; no causal confounding adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: No causal positivity analysis; donor mappings use exact mask strata and the paper audits sparse all-zero replacements, but this assesses perturbation prevalence rather than treatment-effect overlap
counterfactual_validation: None; donor substitution keeps the observed outcome unchanged and is explicitly not validation of an alternative-treatment trajectory
code_access: A public release is promised upon publication; study-specific code is unavailable at the coding cutoff
weights_access: Unavailable; sensitive checkpoints are stated to be excluded from the planned public package
data_access: Credentialed research access to MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD; restricted patient-level tensors, predictions, rosters, and checkpoints are not redistributed
preprocessing_reproducibility: Highly detailed cohort flow, variables, imputation, action alignment, architectures, losses, training stages, checkpoint rules, hardware, evaluation rosters, bootstrap, and cross-database mappings
randomness: Seeds 42, 43, and 44; stochastic donor mappings and hierarchical bootstrap procedures are specified; deterministic algorithms are not enforced
evidence_anchors: Main text pp. 1-7 for claim boundary, model, datasets, replacement audit, results, and limitations; Tables 1-4 pp. 6-7; Appendices B-C pp. 10-20 for cohort, preprocessing, losses, seeds, and checkpoint robustness; Appendix D pp. 21-24 for action audits; Appendices F-H pp. 25-34 for rollout diagnostics, code status, and eICU replication
appraisal_strengths: Strong causal boundary language; detailed action provenance and timing; action-agnostic and perturbation audits; multi-horizon and lead-wise diagnostics; patient-disjoint cross-database replication; extensive statistical robustness
appraisal_limitations: Absolute gains are small and concentrated on MAP; eICU requires retraining and is not site-held-out; binary exposure omits dose and co-interventions; no predictive calibration, clinical decision utility, or causal effect validation; code is not yet public
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: Model-based reinforcement learning for ultrasound-driven autonomous microrobots.
domain: ultrasound-actuated microrobotics; model-based reinforcement learning and autonomous microfluidic navigation
dataset_or_cohort: Self-generated Pygame simulation environments and physical PDMS microfluidic channels with ultrasound-driven microbubble swarms under stagnant and dynamic flow
sample_scale: Millions of simulated training steps, final-50-episode policy evaluations, 6 hours of initial physical training, up to 10 days for scratch physical training, and 30-minute to 3-hour adaptation demonstrations; exact numbers of independent physical trajectories and microrobots are not reported
institution_count: One laboratory experimental setting; no patients or clinical institutions
split_strategy: No conventional fixed train/validation/test split is reported; sequential pretraining across simulated channels is followed by physical adaptation and additional fine-tuning in new channel/flow conditions
observation_process: Camera images acquired at 6-18 frames per second, processed into 64x64 RGB observations with segmentation, cluster detection, CSRT tracking, position, target, size, and environmental geometry
missingness: Tracking loss triggers re-detection or rescue; segmentation masks may be cached; no statistical missing-data model
censoring_or_competing_events: Episodes terminate or reset at target achievement, collision, step threshold, loss of tracking, or radius/shape failure; these are control termination events rather than patient censoring
state: Processed camera image, microrobot position and target coordinates, channel geometry, recurrent deterministic state, and stochastic latent state
observation_decoder: Reconstructed observation, predicted latent state and reward; actor-critic networks use imagined trajectories to choose control actions
action: PZT selection, ultrasound frequency, and peak-to-peak amplitude; discrete, continuous, hybrid, and frequency-sweeping variants are explored
action_provenance: Executed simulated and physical robot commands; amplitude/frequency ranges are informed by manual experiments and an empirical bubble-area amplitude predictor
transition_mechanism: Dreamer v3 recurrent state-space world model with encoder-decoder, recurrent dynamics, reward predictor, latent imagination, and actor-critic policy optimization
maximum_horizon: Multi-step imagined trajectories and real closed-loop episodes continuing until target, collision, or step termination; the exact imagination horizon is not reported
rollout_regime: Free-running latent imagination begins from replay-buffer states; the learned policy is evaluated in simulation and in real closed-loop image-feedback control
capability_claim: Closed-loop planning/control: imagined trajectories train a sequential policy that executes ultrasound commands on real microrobots
baselines: Hyperparameter-tuned PPO, scratch physical training, simulation-pretrained transfer, discrete versus continuous/sweeping action approaches, reward functions, frame-skipping rates, training ratios, and environment-generalization conditions
state_fidelity_metrics: Target success rate, reward, tracked position/velocity, physical image sequences, and qualitative state reconstruction/control behavior; direct latent-state or observation-prediction fidelity is not quantified
transition_metrics: No direct transition-prediction error is reported; evidence is indirect through reward convergence, target success, transfer/adaptation, and real navigation
rollout_stability: Reward and success over training steps and environments; no horizon-resolved imagined-rollout fidelity or model-drift metric
action_sensitivity: Frequency/amplitude/action-space changes, amplitude predictor, sweeping actions, frame skipping, reward variants, and flow-specific action strategies are evaluated; no action-agnostic world-model comparator
calibration_and_uncertainty: Reward variability, standard deviations, IQRs, and smoothing are reported, but no predictive uncertainty calibration or coverage
external_validation: Simulation-to-real and new-channel/flow transfer are demonstrated only with continued training or fine-tuning; this is adapted transfer, not frozen external validation
decision_utility: Real closed-loop target navigation, obstacle avoidance, upstream movement under flow, and recovery; success-rate and reward comparisons are made against PPO
safety_evaluation: Physical-platform hazards are explicitly tested or managed through collision penalties and resets, obstacle and flow stress conditions, overshoot and tracking-loss recovery, ultrasound shutdown, wall/drag constraints, and action-reversal rescue; biological injury, tissue damage, acoustic exposure, and in-vivo safety are not evaluated.
statistical_analysis: Primarily descriptive reward/success curves, means and standard deviations, IQR box plots, and final-50-episode summaries; no inferential confidence intervals or hypothesis tests are reported
causal_language: No medical-treatment counterfactual or causal-effect claim; planning language concerns physical control and expected imagined reward
estimand: Expected discounted policy return and task success under a learned controller; no clinical intervention-effect estimand
confounding_strategy: NA for the control objective; no causal confounding adjustment is claimed
positivity_and_overlap: Action ranges are manually bounded and environment randomization broadens support, but no formal action-coverage or overlap analysis is reported
counterfactual_validation: Real closed-loop control validates task performance, not patient counterfactuals or causal treatment effects
code_access: Public GitHub repository and archived Zenodo code release
weights_access: Public trained checkpoints and reward/trajectory artifacts are reported through Figshare
data_access: Self-generated simulation and physical data, processed CSVs, reward trajectories, success rates, and checkpoints are public through Figshare/GitHub
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed experimental setup, imaging pipeline, reward functions, action ranges, Dreamer components, rescue/reset algorithms, flow simulation, and code/data releases; exact independent physical sample counts and some training-horizon details remain unclear
randomness: PPO hyperparameter results include mean and standard deviation and policies are evaluated over final 50 episodes; exact random seeds and numbers of independent Dreamer/physical runs are not reported
evidence_anchors: Main article pp. 1076-1085 for claims, real control, simulation, transfer, generalization, flow, and discussion; Methods pp. 1085-1088 for state/action/transition and algorithms; Data/Code Availability p. 1088; Extended Data; Supplementary Notes S1-S13, especially S3, S5, S9-S11 for transfer, flow, failures, rescue, generalization, and world-model planning
appraisal_strengths: Peer-reviewed full physical demonstration; real closed-loop planning/control; strong public code/data/checkpoint access; multiple simulated and physical environments; explicit failure/recovery mechanisms and flow/obstacle stress tests
appraisal_limitations: World-model dynamics fidelity and imagination horizon are not directly evaluated; sim-to-real and unseen-environment results require adaptation; exact independent physical sample counts/seeds are unclear; no clinical or in-vivo validation and no predictive uncertainty calibration
source_status: Official peer-reviewed Nature Machine Intelligence version of record and supplementary information inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
domain: robot-assisted prostatectomy video; joint future visual-state and instrument-trajectory forecasting
dataset_or_cohort: SurgWMBench constructed from SAR-RARP50 robot-assisted radical prostatectomy videos, focusing on suturing needle insertion and extraction segments
sample_scale: 1,637 valid segments, 32,740 annotated frames, and one manually annotated 20-point two-dimensional instrument trajectory per segment
institution_count: Underlying institution count and geography are not reported in the inspected paper
split_strategy: The benchmark protocol uses five historical frames/points and fifteen future frames/points; the train/validation/test partition and patient/procedure separation are not reported
observation_process: Regular frame sequences with five observed RGB frames and two-dimensional tool positions followed by fifteen future steps
missingness: No missing-frame or missing-trajectory handling is reported; fixed valid segments are used
censoring_or_competing_events: NA: fixed 20-frame surgical segments without patient censoring or competing-event modeling
state: Frozen SurgMotion visual tokens, embedded historical two-dimensional instrument coordinates, fused temporal-spatial features, and predicted visual-motion history
observation_decoder: Predicted future visual latent grids decoded to RGB by a frozen decoder, plus two-dimensional instrument trajectory points
action: No chosen action is provided as input; the future instrument trajectory is an output described as an action-oriented planning representation, explicitly not a low-level robotic command
action_provenance: Observed/manual annotated instrument motion from recorded surgery; not intended, optimized, or executed model-selected actions
transition_mechanism: Temporal-spatial encoder with separate residual visual and trajectory heads; three-step chunks recursively update a five-step history window
maximum_horizon: Fifteen future frames/trajectory points, generated as five successive three-step chunks
rollout_regime: Scheduled sampling begins during training; validation and test are fully free-running closed loop using predicted visual and trajectory states
capability_claim: Uses world-action and surgical motion-planning language, but the demonstrated capability is passive joint forecasting of observed visual evolution and expert instrument motion; no action-conditioned simulator, action selection, or closed-loop planner is evaluated
baselines: Direct one-shot prediction of all fifteen steps under the same history-only protocol; no external published world-model, trajectory, or strong action-agnostic baseline
state_fidelity_metrics: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS for decoded future frames and ADE/FDE for instrument trajectories, reported in five horizon segments
transition_metrics: Segment-wise visual and trajectory error over t+1:3 through t+13:15
rollout_stability: Free-running segment-wise degradation is quantified across five horizons; both visual fidelity and trajectory accuracy worsen with rollout length
action_sensitivity: None; no action input, action-agnostic comparator, removal, shuffle, timing, magnitude, or chosen-action perturbation
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive distribution, calibration, interval coverage, stochastic rollout analysis, or uncertainty-aware planning
external_validation: No external, temporal, institutional, device, or population validation; one derived benchmark is used
decision_utility: Offline trajectory/visual forecasting is an action-planning proxy only; no robot execution, closed-loop task utility, clinician evaluation, or policy comparison
safety_evaluation: The paper notes that implausible states could be unsafe, but no explicit hazard, constraint violation, failure recovery, subgroup worst-case, or physical safety test is performed
statistical_analysis: Single-run point estimates only; no confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, seed values, or repeated-run variance are reported
causal_language: No causal or counterfactual language; planning relevance is inferred from forecasting observed instrument trajectories and visual consequences
estimand: Observed future visual-state and instrument-trajectory prediction; no treatment effect, policy value, or model-selected action objective
confounding_strategy: NA: no causal claim or adjustment strategy
positivity_and_overlap: NA: no treatment or action-assignment support analysis
counterfactual_validation: None; predictions are compared with recorded future frames and trajectories
code_access: No training code release is established; an anonymized repository is linked only for additional qualitative results
data_access: Underlying SAR-RARP50 is public; processed SurgWMBench annotations, exact split, and final release terms are not established in this paper
preprocessing_reproducibility: Partial: history/horizon construction, architecture, losses, scheduled sampling, optimizer, and metrics are detailed, but split construction, patient separation, seeds, and complete executable preprocessing are unavailable
randomness: Scheduled sampling is stochastic; seed values and repeated independent training runs are not reported
evidence_anchors: Abstract and pp. 2-6 for claim, state/action boundary, architecture, and free-running rollout; Sec. 3 pp. 6-8 and Table 1 for dataset, implementation, and segment metrics; Fig. 2 and conclusion pp. 8-9 for qualitative degradation and limitations
appraisal_strengths: Direct joint evaluation of future visual states and tool trajectories; genuinely free-running fifteen-step rollout; horizon-resolved fidelity and explicit acknowledgment of accumulated error
appraisal_limitations: Planning/action language exceeds demonstrated passive forecasting; no chosen action input or robot control; only a one-shot internal comparator; no split details, repeated-run statistics, uncertainty, external validation, or safety test
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open access
